decisions.reason: After two years this close-to-core rye bread still appears cheap to carry, and while overlap with other loaves raises pruning risk, the cost of keeping the option open remains low.
The medal-winning premium stollen is a revealed winner and flagship seasonal product, so abandoning it would forgo brand value for little gain.
This seeded rye mixed bread fits everyday demand and existing production well, so we keep it as a low-cost assortment option despite some duplication risk.
With two years of market exposure, the dark barley malt rye now looks like the most niche and overlapping bread variant, so we would rationalize it and reallocate the capacity.
The ancient grain bread still offers differentiated artisanal upside, but higher ingredient complexity and uncertain repeat demand make it a more fragile option than standard breads.
